extracted.intended_audience: students and teachers working classroom logic/puzzle activities (math classroom)
extracted.subtask_description: Solve partially filled 10x? suit-grids by reasoning about information revealed by guesses: determine minimal and maximal numbers of additional guesses needed (with example guess choices and revealed suits), and for rows of four boards identify the odd board out with justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best case additional guesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Best case scenario: What is the minimum number of additional guesses needed to complete the board?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assuming that freebies are correctly determined by the guess, give examples of which squares you would guess, and what suits those squares would have to be in order for you to complete the board in this best case scenario. Provide the minimum number (an integer) and exhibit specific guess locations and the suits revealed that achieve completion with that many guesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worst case additional guesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Worst case scenario: What is the maximum number of additional guesses needed to complete the board?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assuming that freebies are correctly determined by the guess, give a sequence of guesses, along with the suits of the revealed squares, that would result in this worst case scenario. Provide the maximum number (an integer) and an explicit ordered list of guess squares and the suits revealed at each step that force completion to require that many guesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Odd-board identification within rows
rubrics_metrics.description: For each row of four boards in Figure 3, indicate which board is not like the others and explain why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each row (i–iv), select the one board that differs and give a clear justification (reasoning about suit-distribution, symmetry, constraints, or other distinguishing properties). State the board label (a/b/c/...) and the rationale that shows it cannot be transformed into the others under the puzzle rules.
